body:
### Description

After #14594, `ubuntu-24.04` sets `Acquire::Retries "1"` and `Acquire::http::Timeout "15"`, so a mirror that stops responding fails over quickly. A mirror that keeps responding very slowly is not covered. `Acquire::http::Timeout` fires only when no data arrives for 15 s, so a trickling transfer never trips it and never fails over to the next entry in `/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt`.

On `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` the package lists download at full speed, then the archives crawl:

```
Fetched 12.5 MB in 1s (10.5 MB/s)
8 upgraded, 187 newly installed, 0 to remove and 38 not upgraded.
Need to get 74.8 MB of archives.
Fetched 74.8 MB in 20min 17s (61.5 kB/s)
```

All 195 archive fetches went to `azure.archive.ubuntu.com`, with no `Err:` or `Ign:` lines and no retries. On 2026-09-30 the same install took 20m45s, 17m03s, 15m04s and 9m33s in four of seven runs of one public workflow, and 40–80 s in the other three.

We now serve these archives from an Actions cache, with each file checked against the index's SHA256, so this no longer blocks us. We are reporting it because the #14594 fix does not reach this case. apt has no minimum-throughput setting, so the fix probably has to be on the mirror side, as with the degraded node GitHub Support found in #14594, or a wrapper that restarts a slow fetch on the next mirror.

### Platforms affected

- [ ] Azure DevOps
- [x] GitHub Actions - Standard Runners
- [ ] GitHub Actions - Larger Runners

### Runner images affected

- [x] Ubuntu 24.04

### Image version and build link

Image `ubuntu-24.04`, version `20260920.314.1` (runner image provisioner `20260828.587`).
Run: https://github.com/stigmer/stigmer/actions/runs/36742113867, job `ts-workspace / Desktop Rust Check`, step `Install Tauri's Linux packages`.

### Is it regression?

No. It is a case #14594's timeout change does not cover.

### Expected behavior

A mirror serving archives at a small fraction of normal speed is abandoned for the next mirror in `/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt`, as a stalled one is. The install finishes in about a minute.

### Actual behavior

apt stays on the slow mirror for the whole download: 74.8 MB at 61.5 kB/s, 20 minutes.

### Repro steps

It happens intermittently; four of seven runs were affected on 2026-09-30.

1. On `ubuntu-24.04`: `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf`.
2. When the pool routes the fetch to a slow `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` node, the step runs 9–20 minutes, with `Fetched ... (61.5 kB/s)` at the end and no errors.
title: [Ubuntu] apt stays on a slow azure.archive.ubuntu.com node for 20 min; the #14594 timeout only covers stalls
